Delete Candidates

  • [P3][delete] Remove unused framework kz metadata. _framework.py:289–301, :656–659, :754 store and forward Wave.kz / TMatrix.kz, but no numerical path reads either. Cylindrical field, cross-section and periodic-conversion paths read basis.kz; public cylinder constructors explicitly promise fixed axial labels. Delete those constructor parameters/attributes and forwarding at :214 and :754. Retain Backend.multilayer(kz=...), which feeds diff.cylinder.
  • [P3][unneeded] Remove the constant polarization parameter from Backend.multilayer. _framework.py:183–190: all six callers in advect.py, jax.py, and torch.py pass "helicity" and then perform the requested conversion themselves. Delete this private parameter, unreachable rejection branch, and six constant arguments. Public helicity/parity behavior remains unchanged.

Merge Candidates

  • [P3][merge] Share the framework-independent namespace functions. The stack implementations at advect.py:1690–1697, jax.py:494–501, and torch.py:481–488 are identical and do not use their module backend. Keep one implementation in _framework.py and explicitly re-export it from each namespace. Likewise, the three solve_periodic functions only forward unchanged arguments to _framework.solve_periodic; direct re-exports preserve their signatures. support.py:338–373 already discovers explicit re-exports, so this needs no new catalog machinery. Regenerate API documentation afterward.

Workarounds For Unapproved Behavior

  • None substantiated. Dynamic medium/frequency compatibility checks, outgoing-wave restrictions, diffraction matching, and precision checks enforce documented physical or adapter contracts; deleting them would weaken correctness.

Overbuilt Tests

  • None worth blocking merge. The shared three-framework fixture exercises physical outputs and derivatives rather than merely mirroring constructors. Retain the scientific evaluation records and harness provenance.

No Safe Simplifications

  • No further meaningful deletion identified in _physics.py or the reviewed evaluation launch/watch paths. Most thin physical wrappers provide the intended named arguments and metadata boundaries.

Read-only source/caller review only; no tests, builds, file writes, Git changes, or external actions. These are optional cleanup findings, not merge blockers.
